title: Book One · Chapter 136: Four Pictures and a Race
story:
The list takes longer than Ronan thinks.

He writes four picture names. Then Leo comes to the kitchen and says the map is not one picture. It is two roads and a key. The map has little marks. The key explains each mark.

“It still goes on one sheet,” Ronan says.

“A large sheet.”

Mum gives them two small pieces of paper. “Put the size beside the name.”

They lay the drawings on the floor. There is not enough floor. Ronan moves his shoes. Leo moves a chair. Mum asks them to keep a clear way to the cooker.

The boys measure each sheet with string. They do not know all the sizes. They cut paper strips as long as the edges. Each strip shows the length of one side. Miss Wu can see the real sizes that way.

Then they come to the race.

Leo wants the race to start outside the room. Runners would go round the yard. They would finish beside the pictures. He draws an arrow so long that it goes off the sheet.

“People may be coming in,” Ronan says.

“They can stand back.”

“Some are old.”

“They can stand back slowly.”

Ronan tries not to laugh. He does not want Leo to think he agrees.

Mum puts a bowl of water on the table. She has vegetables to wash. The boys lift their papers out of the way.

“You want a race,” she says. “Who will watch the runners? You must ask someone.”

Leo adds TEACHER under the arrow.

“Which teacher?” Ronan asks.

Leo looks towards the yard. “We could ask.”

On Monday Miss Wu looks at the pictures, the strips, and the race. She gives the race its own little place on the desk.

“I can help with a quiet room,” she says. “I cannot also run a race.”

Leo says nothing. Ronan looks at the long arrow.

“Could it be another day?” he asks.

“Perhaps, with the right teacher. It is a different event.”

She asks about the pictures next. Mr Qiu agreed to the old classroom wall. He has not agreed to visits from families. Mum wants to see the new words first. Then she will decide about her drawing. Mei has not been asked at all.

Ronan reads the list again. They need more answers first. Miss Wu is not cross. She marks some lines on the list. They must ask about each of those.

“This helps us know the work,” she says. “Now we can see all the work. The list helps us.”

Miss Wu lets them look through the little room's window. There are stacked chairs inside and a long plain table. Leo points to the open floor. The floor looks wide enough now. Then Miss Wu asks them to think about twenty visitors. They would all need space to stand. Ronan puts his own two feet together. If twenty people come in, the room will look full. They cannot use all the space for tables.

After school Leo sits on a step with the race sheet. Ronan sits beside him.

“I still want something people can do,” Leo says.

“They can look.”

“Walls can look at pictures all day.”

Ronan thinks. He takes the small map from his bag and lays it between them.

“They could find places on this. They can walk and look.”

Leo puts his finger on the bend. “A street game.”

He turns the race sheet over. On the clean side he begins to draw three little doors. Ronan watches him draw the first door. Leo is not asking about the race now. He wants to try making a street game.

---

重点表达：key＝图例；measure＝测量；event＝活动。

情节提示：strip＝纸条；stacked chairs＝叠放的椅子；cooker＝炉灶。

理解：1. 为什么展示不能直接加一场赛跑？2. Leo 想到什么新的参与方式？
